reason: The pediatric disparity commentary relates diagnosis/treatment distribution to socioeconomic circumstances and proposes insurance/service barriers. This supports only a narrower socioeconomic care-inequity pathway; it does not measure SES causing access to evaluation at age eight.

The pediatric commentary identifies inadequate insurance coverage as a possible contributor to diagnostic and treatment problems. This supplies clinical support for a financial-access barrier, but does not measure household income, affordability or a controlled age-eight access effect.

The commentary describes socioeconomic disparities in pediatric diagnosis and treatment. This supports uneven treatment provision, but does not demonstrate that higher SES causes treatment continuity or establish an age-eight-specific effect.

The adult bipolar study documents symptom overlap and recommends assessment for coexisting ADHD/BSD. This supports diagnostic ambiguity as a clinical mechanism, but neither screening positivity nor overlap demonstrates actual misdiagnosis, and no age-32 error-rate effect is estimated.

The systematic medication review reports short-term QOL improvement in adults. QOL reflects perceived functioning and provides narrower treatment-benefit evidence, but is not a separately measured general functional-impairment outcome, and adult studies are few with no age-45 estimate.
